primary.title: Worth Wandering: The Public Domain Review
primary.summary: The Public Domain Review is an independent, nonprofit journal exploring the strange, beautiful and often forgotten things humanity has created, from medieval manuscripts and Victorian photography to early films, unusual scientific theories, recordings of people long gone and an enormous collection of art that belongs to everyone.

primary.title: /groundwork: a skill that makes any repo runnable from a fresh clone
primary.summary: Most repos only run on the machines of the few developers who set them up. /groundwork is an agent skill that finds the missing env files, databases and docs, then fixes them.

primary.title: Pros and Cons of Self-hosting a Public Git Forge
primary.summary: It's been over a year since I mostly broke up with GitHub . In that year, I've been running my own public Forgejo instance for my personal projects. It's important to stress the public part, as most of what I'm going to discuss is directly correlated to that. This isn't a post to critique Forgejo vs. alternatives, either. I found Forgejo to be great. My only gripe is that I very much prefer GitLab
